title: Aunque: borders on the map, life on the ground

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know concessive clauses with *aunque* from A2 Unit 28. They join two ideas that seem to pull against each other. In this lesson the contrast is between what an official map or a state claimed and what people really did.

sections.title: Aunque + indicative
rows: Aunque los mapas mostraban una línea, las personas la cruzaban.
the map says one thing, people do another
Aunque Paraguay luchó durante años, perdió la guerra.
the effort did not change the result
La idea oficial era clara, aunque la realidad era más complicada.
*aunque* can also come in the middle

items.spanish: Aunque había una frontera, muchas familias seguían juntas.
items.english: Although there was a border, many families stayed together.

items.spanish: Aunque Bolivia perdió la costa, siguió siendo un país.
items.english: Although Bolivia lost its coast, it stayed a country.

items.spanish: Los mapas mostraban una línea, aunque la vida seguía igual.
items.english: The maps showed a line, although life went on as before.

items.spanish: Aunque las escuelas enseñaban símbolos nacionales, las familias hablaban su idioma.
items.english: Although the schools taught national symbols, families spoke their own language.

sections.content: After *aunque* use the indicative for something that is a fact (*aunque había una frontera*). *Aunque* can start the sentence (with a comma after the first part) or come after the main clause. *A pesar de que* means almost the same and is a little more formal.
